question: She said, "I am happy today." Change to Indirect Speech.
options: A) She said that she was happy that day.
B) She said that she is happy today.
C) She told that she was happy today.
D) She said that I was happy that day.
correct_answer: A) She said that she was happy that day.
explanation: In indirect speech, 'said' remains 'said', 'I' changes to 'she', 'am' changes to 'was', and 'today' changes to 'that day'.

question: He said, "I will go to school tomorrow." Change to Indirect Speech.
options: A) He said that he will go to school the next day.
B) He said that he would go to school the next day.
C) He said that he would go to school tomorrow.
D) He told that he will go to school tomorrow.
correct_answer: B) He said that he would go to school the next day.
explanation: 'Will' changes to 'would' in indirect speech, and 'tomorrow' changes to 'the next day'. 'Said' remains 'said' when no object is present.

question: She said to me, "You are my best friend." Change to Indirect Speech.
options: A) She told me that I was her best friend.
B) She said to me that you were her best friend.
C) She told me that you are her best friend.
D) She said me that I was her best friend.
correct_answer: A) She told me that I was her best friend.
explanation: 'Said to me' changes to 'told me', 'you' changes to 'I' (referring to the listener), and 'are' changes to 'was'.

question: He said, "I have finished my homework." Change to Indirect Speech.
options: A) He said that he has finished his homework.
B) He said that he had finished his homework.
C) He told that he finished his homework.
D) He said that he have finished his homework.
correct_answer: B) He said that he had finished his homework.
explanation: Present perfect 'have finished' changes to past perfect 'had finished' in indirect speech. 'My' changes to 'his'.

question: She said, "I was reading a book." Change to Indirect Speech.
options: A) She said that she was reading a book.
B) She said that she had been reading a book.
C) She said that she is reading a book.
D) She told that she was reading a book.
correct_answer: B) She said that she had been reading a book.
explanation: Past continuous 'was reading' changes to past perfect continuous 'had been reading' in indirect speech.

question: Ram said to Sita, "Please help me." Change to Indirect Speech.
options: A) Ram requested Sita to help him.
B) Ram told Sita to please help him.
C) Ram said to Sita to help him.
D) Ram requested Sita that please help him.
correct_answer: A) Ram requested Sita to help him.
explanation: For requests with 'please', use 'requested' as the reporting verb and convert to infinitive form. 'Me' changes to 'him'.

question: The teacher said, "The earth revolves around the sun." Change to Indirect Speech.
options: A) The teacher said that the earth revolved around the sun.
B) The teacher said that the earth revolves around the sun.
C) The teacher told that the earth had revolved around the sun.
D) The teacher said that the earth is revolving around the sun.
correct_answer: B) The teacher said that the earth revolves around the sun.
explanation: Universal truths and scientific facts do not change tense in indirect speech. The present tense 'revolves' remains unchanged.

question: He said, "I can swim very well." Change to Indirect Speech.
options: A) He said that he can swim very well.
B) He said that he could swim very well.
C) He told that he can swim very well.
D) He said that he may swim very well.
correct_answer: B) He said that he could swim very well.
explanation: 'Can' changes to 'could' in indirect speech when the reporting verb is in past tense.

question: She said, "I may attend the party." Change to Indirect Speech.
options: A) She said that she may attend the party.
B) She said that she might attend the party.
C) She told that she may attend the party.
D) She said that she would attend the party.
correct_answer: B) She said that she might attend the party.
explanation: 'May' changes to 'might' in indirect speech when the reporting verb is in past tense.

question: He said to her, "Do you like coffee?" Change to Indirect Speech.
options: A) He asked her if she liked coffee.
B) He asked her that she liked coffee.
C) He said to her if she liked coffee.
D) He asked her whether she likes coffee.
correct_answer: A) He asked her if she liked coffee.
explanation: Yes/No questions use 'if' or 'whether' in indirect speech. 'Said to' changes to 'asked', and 'like' changes to 'liked'.

question: She said, "What is your name?" Change to Indirect Speech.
options: A) She asked what my name was.
B) She asked what was my name.
C) She asked what is my name.
D) She said what my name was.
correct_answer: A) She asked what my name was.
explanation: Wh-questions in indirect speech follow subject-verb order (not inverted). 'Is' changes to 'was' and 'your' changes to 'my'.

question: The officer said to the soldier, "Stand at ease." Change to Indirect Speech.
options: A) The officer ordered the soldier to stand at ease.
B) The officer told the soldier stand at ease.
C) The officer said to the soldier to stand at ease.
D) The officer commanded the soldier that stand at ease.
correct_answer: A) The officer ordered the soldier to stand at ease.
explanation: Imperative sentences (commands) use 'ordered/commanded' as reporting verb and convert to infinitive form.

question: She said, "I lived here two years ago." Change to Indirect Speech.
options: A) She said that she had lived there two years before.
B) She said that she lived there two years ago.
C) She said that she has lived there two years before.
D) She told that she lived here two years ago.
correct_answer: A) She said that she had lived there two years before.
explanation: Simple past 'lived' changes to past perfect 'had lived'. 'Here' changes to 'there' and 'ago' changes to 'before'.

question: He said, "I am going to the market now." Change to Indirect Speech.
options: A) He said that he was going to the market then.
B) He said that he is going to the market now.
C) He told that he was going to the market now.
D) He said that he went to the market then.
correct_answer: A) He said that he was going to the market then.
explanation: Present continuous 'am going' changes to past continuous 'was going'. 'Now' changes to 'then'.

question: She said to him, "Don't make noise." Change to Indirect Speech.
options: A) She told him not to make noise.
B) She said to him not to make noise.
C) She told him don't make noise.
D) She requested him not to make noise.
correct_answer: A) She told him not to make noise.
explanation: Negative imperatives use 'told + not + to + verb'. 'Said to' changes to 'told' when an object is present.

question: He said, "I must complete this task." Change to Indirect Speech.
options: A) He said that he must complete that task.
B) He said that he had to complete that task.
C) He said that he should complete that task.
D) He told that he must complete this task.
correct_answer: B) He said that he had to complete that task.
explanation: 'Must' changes to 'had to' in indirect speech when expressing obligation. 'This' changes to 'that'.

question: She said, "How beautiful this flower is!" Change to Indirect Speech.
options: A) She exclaimed that the flower was very beautiful.
B) She said how beautiful that flower was.
C) She exclaimed how beautiful this flower is.
D) She told that the flower is very beautiful.
correct_answer: A) She exclaimed that the flower was very beautiful.
explanation: Exclamatory sentences use 'exclaimed' as reporting verb. 'How beautiful' is replaced by 'very beautiful' and 'this' changes to 'the'.

question: He said, "Hurrah! We have won the match." Change to Indirect Speech.
options: A) He exclaimed with joy that they had won the match.
B) He said hurrah that they had won the match.
C) He exclaimed that they have won the match.
D) He told with joy that they won the match.
correct_answer: A) He exclaimed with joy that they had won the match.
explanation: 'Hurrah' indicates joy, so use 'exclaimed with joy'. 'We' changes to 'they' and 'have won' changes to 'had won'.

question: She said, "Alas! I have lost my purse." Change to Indirect Speech.
options: A) She exclaimed with sorrow that she had lost her purse.
B) She said alas that she had lost her purse.
C) She exclaimed with joy that she had lost her purse.
D) She told with sorrow that she lost her purse.
correct_answer: A) She exclaimed with sorrow that she had lost her purse.
explanation: 'Alas' indicates sorrow/grief, so use 'exclaimed with sorrow'. 'My' changes to 'her' and 'have lost' changes to 'had lost'.

question: He said to me, "Where do you live?" Change to Indirect Speech.
options: A) He asked me where I lived.
B) He asked me where do I live.
C) He said to me where I lived.
D) He asked me where did I live.
correct_answer: A) He asked me where I lived.
explanation: Wh-questions use 'asked' as reporting verb. The question form changes to statement form (subject before verb). 'You' changes to 'I'.

question: She said, "I will be playing cricket tomorrow." Change to Indirect Speech.
options: A) She said that she would be playing cricket the next day.
B) She said that she will be playing cricket the next day.
C) She told that she would play cricket tomorrow.
D) She said that she would have played cricket the next day.
correct_answer: A) She said that she would be playing cricket the next day.
explanation: Future continuous 'will be playing' changes to 'would be playing'. 'Tomorrow' changes to 'the next day'.

question: He said, "I had already eaten dinner." Change to Indirect Speech.
options: A) He said that he had already eaten dinner.
B) He said that he has already eaten dinner.
C) He told that he had already eaten dinner.
D) He said that he already ate dinner.
correct_answer: A) He said that he had already eaten dinner.
explanation: Past perfect 'had eaten' remains past perfect 'had eaten' in indirect speech — it does not change further.

question: She said to him, "Are you feeling well?" Change to Indirect Speech.
options: A) She asked him if he was feeling well.
B) She asked him whether he is feeling well.
C) She said to him if he was feeling well.
D) She asked him that he was feeling well.
correct_answer: A) She asked him if he was feeling well.
explanation: Yes/No questions use 'if/whether'. 'Said to' becomes 'asked'. 'Are feeling' changes to 'was feeling' and 'you' changes to 'he'.

question: He said, "I should study harder." Change to Indirect Speech.
options: A) He said that he should study harder.
B) He said that he shall study harder.
C) He told that he should study harder.
D) He said that he would study harder.
correct_answer: A) He said that he should study harder.
explanation: 'Should' does not change in indirect speech. It remains 'should' regardless of the tense of the reporting verb.

question: She said, "I bought this dress yesterday." Change to Indirect Speech.
options: A) She said that she had bought that dress the previous day.
B) She said that she bought that dress yesterday.
C) She told that she had bought this dress the previous day.
D) She said that she has bought that dress the previous day.
correct_answer: A) She said that she had bought that dress the previous day.
explanation: Simple past 'bought' changes to past perfect 'had bought'. 'This' changes to 'that' and 'yesterday' changes to 'the previous day'.

question: He said to her, "I love you." Change to Indirect Speech.
options: A) He told her that he loved her.
B) He said to her that he loved her.
C) He told her that I love you.
D) He said that he loved her.
correct_answer: A) He told her that he loved her.
explanation: 'Said to her' changes to 'told her'. 'I' changes to 'he' and 'you' changes to 'her'. 'Love' changes to 'loved'.

question: She said, "I will have completed the project by Monday." Change to Indirect Speech.
options: A) She said that she would have completed the project by Monday.
B) She said that she will have completed the project by Monday.
C) She told that she would complete the project by Monday.
D) She said that she had completed the project by Monday.
correct_answer: A) She said that she would have completed the project by Monday.
explanation: Future perfect 'will have completed' changes to 'would have completed' in indirect speech.

question: He said, "I used to play football in school." Change to Indirect Speech.
options: A) He said that he used to play football in school.
B) He said that he had used to play football in school.
C) He told that he used to play football in school.
D) He said that he would play football in school.
correct_answer: A) He said that he used to play football in school.
explanation: 'Used to' does not change in indirect speech. It remains 'used to' regardless of the reporting verb tense.

question: She said to me, "Come here immediately." Change to Indirect Speech.
options: A) She told me to go there immediately.
B) She said to me to come here immediately.
C) She ordered me to come here immediately.
D) She told me to come here immediately.
correct_answer: A) She told me to go there immediately.

question: He said, "I know the answer." Change to Indirect Speech.
options: A) He said that he knew the answer.

correct_answer: A) He said that he knew the answer.

question: She said, "I will not lie to you." Change to Indirect Speech.

correct_answer: A) She said that she would not lie to me.

question: He said to his friend, "Let us go for a walk." Change to Indirect Speech.
options: A) He proposed to his friend that they should go for a walk.
B) He told his friend to go for a walk.
C) He said to his friend that let them go for a walk.

correct_answer: A) He proposed to his friend that they should go for a walk.
explanation: 'Let us' in direct speech becomes 'proposed/suggested that they should' in indirect speech.

question: She said, "I have been working here for five years." Change to Indirect Speech.
options: A) She said that she had been working there for five years.

explanation: Present perfect continuous 'have been working' changes to past perfect continuous 'had been working'. 'Here' changes to 'there'.

question: She said to me, "Thank you for your help." Change to Indirect Speech.
